name: monitor
description: System monitoring tool for multiple computers — local, SSH, EC2. Local state lives at the effective monitor home (~/.hasna/monitor by default, resolved via @hasna/paths; the XDG data home is adopted only once the store is migrated there or HASNA_DATA_HOME is set).

serviceSurfaces.name: http-api
serviceSurfaces.deferReason: monitor-serve (previously monitor-server) serves a local REST/SSE surface today, but it declares neither GET /ready nor GET /version and ships no generated SDK, so it is not yet a contract-supported API surface.

waivedStorageEngines.reason: src/db/postgres-adapter.ts exists but cannot serve traffic: its runSync helper busy-waits with Bun.sleepSync, which blocks the event loop the pending query needs, so every call times out after 30s. Declaring postgresql as a supported engine would be false until that adapter is rewritten async-first.

conformanceBaseline.reason: The two bins below fall outside the contract bin allowlist and cannot be declared yet: monitor-serve flips a cli-with-store manifest to service-capable (invalidating the sqlite-only storage waiver until the storage rewrite lands), and monitor-server is its one-release deprecated shim awaiting the next breaking release (monitor-web was dropped by the dashboard-removal wave). The canonical `monitor serve` subcommand exists; the standalone bins are a published-package breaking change. `bun run contract-baseline` holds this entry's exact text as the authority in CI. Remove or narrow an entry as soon as its cause is resolved.

failures.detail: in package.json but undeclared: monitor-serve, monitor-server

pendingBinRenames.reason: Canonical server bin shipped by the fleet naming wave (hasna/apps#1602); it falls outside the contract bin allowlist for now because declaring a -serve bin flips a cli-with-store manifest to service-capable and invalidates the sqlite-only storage waiver (storage rewrite + /ready /version surface first).
Deprecated alias of monitor-serve (same entrypoint, bins/monitor-server.js). Kept installed for one release so published consumers do not break; drop it in the next breaking release.
